target_customer: Families and adults hiring private tutors, plus tutors who pay a commission
problem: Finding a vetted local tutor meant agencies like Sylvan or unvetted Craigslist; Tutorspree matched people with screened private tutors online.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (50 percent commission on a tutor's first lesson, decreasing after)

founders.name: Aaron Harris
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch 2011, 2013 and 2014. YC page says he later became a YC partner.

founders.name: Ryan Bednar
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; later CEO of RankScience (W17).

founders.name: Josh Abrams
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch 2011-01 and 2014-01; no bio found.

exit.reason: The co-founders cited a crowded market, difficulty scaling a local marketplace and slower than expected growth; they closed the company around September 2013, returned remaining capital to investors, and WyzAnt bought the remaining assets in an undisclosed asset purchase.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two-sided marketplace with tutor screening and booking; the TechCrunch launch coverage describes no hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Local supply of tutors gave some network effect, but growth was slow and WyzAnt, TakeLessons and Tutor.com competed for the same tutors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WyzAnt raised $21.5M in December 2013 and bought Tutorspree's assets in January 2014 after it had shut down.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2011-12-20) reported about 3,000 tutors with a waiting list of over 6,000 and many users beyond students, showing demand for private tutoring; later coverage said the model struggled to scale locally.

branding.domain_note: Used tutorspree.com (exact .com); it now redirects to wyzant.com after the asset sale.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched in TechCrunch as an Airbnb for tutoring

branding.brand_signature: Airbnb for tutoring framing in press
branding.community_and_virality: A TUTORSPREE trademark was filed 2013-01-11 by Tutorspree, Inc. (Justia).

brand_strength.rationale: Steady launch and funding coverage and the Airbnb for tutoring label, but no sign the name drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Tutorspree launched in January 2011 from YC W11, raised $1M led by Sequoia in December 2011 and $800K in February 2013 for about $1.8M total, and reached over 7,000 tutors with 10 employees. The founders said the market was crowded and a local marketplace was hard to scale with slower growth than expected, so they shut down around September 2013 and returned capital; WyzAnt bought the assets in January 2014. Competition from WyzAnt and TakeLessons and failure to scale local supply and demand explain the end.
notes: The YC page shows team size 51 and a description mentioning Wyzant, apparently copied from the acquirer; the YC page also puts the company in Chicago while other sources say New York. The 2013 round: the Form D suggested $1.9M and TheCompanyCheck lists $2.9M total; TechCrunch says $800K closed within a larger ongoing round and a $1.8M total, which the company confirmed in 2014. The 2013 stage label is not stated by the article, so it is other. Status Inactive agrees with the asset acquisition after shutdown. The TNW April 2011 article was not opened. Founders' prior employers and education beyond Bednar's SeatGeek were not found.
